{{short description|Theorem in algebra}}
In algebra, '''Posner's theorem''' states that given a [[prime ring|prime]] [[polynomial identity algebra]] ''A'' with center ''Z'', the ring <math>A \otimes_Z Z_{(0)}</math> is a [[central simple algebra]] over <math>Z_{(0)}</math>, the [[field of fractions]] of ''Z''.<ref>{{harvnb|Artin|1999|loc=Theorem V. 8.1.}}</ref> It is named after [[Ed Posner]].
